cards.title: Who hurts
cards.description: Fool: whose pain, what we are testing
cards.prompt:
State whose problem we are testing. Analysis only — no product, no code.

Output:
1. Target audience (specific, not “everyone”)
2. Observable problem
3. How people cope today
4. Hypothesis: “If we do X for Y, then Z changes”
5. What must be proven before building
6. Open questions

If input is thin — at most 3 questions. Mark unknowns as assumptions.
Forbidden: inventing users, quotes, demand, market; suggesting code or features.

Next: card “How to test”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — enough input for a test plan
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — user answers required

cards.title: How to test
cards.description: Hierophant: cheapest method, metric, stop rule
cards.prompt:
Write the cheapest plan to test the hypothesis from “Who hurts”. Lock the plan BEFORE any experiment.

Rules:
- AI research and chat opinions are not proof. Proof: interviews, signups, clicks, preorders.
- One method: interview / landing / fake door / waitlist / preorder / post / survey.
- If an existing product already solves it — also run “What exists”.
- Without a threshold the plan is not ready. Do not change the threshold later.
- If the method needs money or ads — warn first.

Output: hypothesis · method · metric · threshold (number) · deadline · what FAIL means · what the human does.
Example thresholds: 5 interviews in 7 days; 10 signups in 5 days; 2 preorders or contacts.

Do not write product code. Do not invent numbers.
Next: “Ask people” or “Mini test” — per chosen method.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — plan and threshold set
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — not enough data for a plan

cards.title: Ask people
cards.description: Two of Cups: interviews without invented people
cards.prompt:
Work in one mode only.

Mode 1 — real interview notes exist. Analyze only those: pains, workarounds, frequency, evidence of willingness to pay or act, disconfirming facts, how many talks, whether the “How to test” threshold is met.

Mode 2 — no answers yet. Prepare 7–10 questions and instructions: ask about the last time, frequency, cost, current tool; do not ask “would you buy?”; do not pitch the idea; need at least 3–5 real conversations.

Forbidden: inventing respondents or quotes; mixing modes; treating chat opinions as proof.

If answers are thin — keep collecting. If they kill the hypothesis — “Change the idea”. If enough — “What exists” or “Verdict”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — enough real answers for the next step
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — no or too few answers

cards.title: What exists
cards.description: Wheel: competitors, open source, what to reuse
cards.prompt:
Find what already solves this problem. Do not reinvent the wheel.

1. Competitors (2–4): what they do, weak spot, what proves demand. No competitors is suspicious: niche, new problem, or unimportant problem. Competitors exist = market exists — not a fail.
2. Open source (2–4 repos): what to reuse, license, freshness, risk, what NOT to copy. No web access — ask for links; do not guess names. Do not paste third-party code.
3. Substitutes: spreadsheets, chats, manual work — what works and what breaks.

Verdict: reuse ready-made / reuse partly / market unclear.
Do not write product code. Next: “Mini test” or “Verdict”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — analysis based on data or user links
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — links or facts required

cards.title: Mini test
cards.description: Magician: smoke / fake door / waitlist with a fixed threshold
cards.prompt:
Build the smallest demand check using the threshold from “How to test”. One format: landing with a form; fake door; waitlist; preorder; post or survey in a relevant chat.

Do not change the threshold. Create files only if the user explicitly asked for a landing. Otherwise text only: headline, CTA, how to count. No payments, no production deploy. Do not promise what does not exist; “soon” / “early access” is fine.

Do not invent clicks or signups. No results yet — tell them to run the test and return with numbers. Results exist — “Verdict”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — results can be judged
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — the test still must be run

cards.title: Verdict
cards.description: Justice: only real facts → PASS or FAIL
cards.prompt:
Decide: continue or not. Judge ONLY what the user actually gave: notes, sourced numbers, links, screenshots, chat logs.

One rule: compare to the threshold from “How to test”.
- threshold met → PASS;
- threshold missed, no facts, number without source, no threshold, or data for the wrong hypothesis → FAIL.
Chat opinions and AI research are not proof. Do not PASS out of pity or because “the idea is good”.

List evidence, threshold, and gaps first — then the decision.
PASS → specification. FAIL → “Change the idea”. No threshold → “How to test”.

The project may be empty — no fact = not PASS.
Forbidden: inventing evidence; PASSing out of pity or because “the idea is good”; flattery.

End with exactly two lines:
KEYCODE_GATE: PASS
KEYCODE_NEXT: spec-v1/brief

or:
KEYCODE_GATE: FAIL
KEYCODE_NEXT: validate-v1/pivot

cards.title: Change the idea
cards.description: Hanged Man: shrink audience / problem / channel; keep facts
cards.prompt:
The check failed. Change only one part; keep the facts.

Pick one: shrink audience; shrink problem; change channel; reuse ready-made instead of building.
Two–three pivots without new data — stop: continuing is pointless. No facts — go back to “Who hurts”. If the user wants to change everything at once — ask them to pick one.

Output: what stays true · what changes · new hypothesis · next step (“How to test” / “Ask people” / “What exists” / “Mini test”).
Do not write code. Do not invent facts to justify the pivot.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — new hypothesis and next step are clear
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: BLOCKED — continuing is pointless; no new facts

cards.title: Checklist
cards.description: World: run the check per plan; stop without real data
cards.prompt:
Run the idea check with what is already known.

Required:
1. problem stated (“Who hurts”);
2. plan with threshold (“How to test”);
3. the method chosen in the plan was actually done (interview and/or mini test — not both required);
4. competitors/open source if that affects the decision;
5. threshold met.

Missing real data for a required item — do not PASS; send back to that card. Do not invent data. Same item fails 2–3 times — change method, shrink the idea, or stop.

Final PASS only if the threshold is closed with facts.

The project may be empty — no fact = not PASS.
Forbidden: inventing evidence; PASSing out of pity or because “the idea is good”; flattery.

End with exactly two lines:
KEYCODE_GATE: PASS
KEYCODE_NEXT: spec-v1/brief

or:
KEYCODE_GATE: FAIL
KEYCODE_NEXT: validate-v1/evidence-plan

(if you know the missing card — replace evidence-plan with problem, interview, market, experiment, or pivot)

cards.title: Recap
cards.description: High Priestess: hypothesis / evidence / gaps / next
cards.prompt:
Read this chat. Do not write or change code. Do not invent evidence.

Four short blocks (1–3 bullets each):
1. Hypothesis
2. Evidence (only what exists)
3. Gaps
4. Next step — one card: Who hurts / How to test / Ask people / What exists / Mini test / Verdict / Change the idea / Checklist

The project may be empty — write only what is visible in chat.
Forbidden: inventing completed work; writing or changing code; adding KEYCODE_SCORE, KEYCODE_GATE, KEYCODE_NEXT, or KEYCODE_STATUS lines.

Do not add KEYCODE_SCORE, KEYCODE_GATE, KEYCODE_NEXT, or KEYCODE_STATUS lines.
